thread:
frank: Heads-up: customer reported a tenant suddenly lost a bunch of feature overrides during a deploy window. Looks like deleted overrides reappeared briefly then disappeared again.

nina: That smells like a snapshot vs apply race. Snapshot loader writes a full snapshot and then apply-service replays deltas; if snapshot is older than last-write we might rehydrate deleted keys.

leo: We saw similar once where tombstones were not persisted through the snapshot because garbage-collector pruned them early. Do we have tombstone semantics today?

anya: currently deletes are represented as tombstone rows with deleted_at, but snapshot compressor folds them away after 24h to save space. If apply replay is delayed, a snapshot that excludes tombstones can reintroduce keys.

frank: Oof. So two levers: keep tombstones longer or make snapshots incremental with watermark.

nina: Also we can add a signed snapshot watermark: snapshot carries last_seen_op_ts and apply ignores snapshot entries whose key has a newer op in ops-log. Might be cheaper than increasing tombstone TTL.

leo: Good idea. We should also add a quick metric: count of keys rehydrated by snapshot vs keys created by normal apply. That will surface regression.

anya: Short term mitigation: for the next 48h we'll extend tombstone TTL to 7 days for tenants > enterprise tier. Low-risk and reversible.

product-bot: Note: customer-impacting bug reported by Acme Inc (INC-2345).

frank: Rollout plan: 1) extend TTL in staging and run 24h soak, 2) add snapshot watermark guard behind flag `snapshot.verify_watermark`, dry-run for 2 days, 3) revert tombstone TTL if watermark works.

nina: For the watermark approach, apply-service needs quick lookup of ops-log highwater for tenant during snapshot load. If highwater > snapshot.last_seen_op_ts then drop keys from snapshot that have no tombstone but have later ops.

leo: Implementation note: ops-log lookup must be bounded latency. We'll cache tenant-highwater in memory with a 30s TTL. That should be fine.

anya: Migration note: Compressor job must include snapshot.last_seen_op_ts in metadata. Also record compressor version.

frank: Telemetry to add: `snapshot.rehydrated_keys` (counter), `snapshot.discarded_keys_due_to_watermark` (counter), and an alert if rehydrated_keys_rate > 0.1% of tenant keys in any 1h window.

nina: Runbook: if alert fires, rollback snapshot-verification flag and increase tombstone TTL, then investigate rehydration logs: `select * from snapshot_rehydrate where tenant_id=... order by ts desc limit 50`.

leo: Tests: add a deterministic concurrency unit test that simulates snapshot at t1, delete at t2, compressor run that omits tombstone, apply replay at t3. Expected: final state no key.

anya: ops-bot: queued patch: staging compressor now writes last_seen_op_ts (build/8901).

frank: I'll open PR for watermark-guard today and land behind flag.

product-bot: FYI PMs notified and asked for customer-facing summary.

nina: One more edge: structured overrides (maps) where child keys deleted but parent snapshot still has older map. Watermark logic must operate at leaf key granularity.

leo: ack. We'll normalize keys to flattened path in the snapshot index so guard works per-path.

ops-bot: deploy: staging watermark-guard flag added (runtime/3456).

frank: Thanks. Schedule post-mortem doc and add a short confluence note under infra/runbooks/config-snapshot-race.

anya: I'll draft the post-mortem and include suggested follow-ups: long-term: compacted-op-log with tombstone retention guarantees, and UI indicator for "recently deleted" keys.

frank: Great. Keep updates here and ping if alert fires. :pray:
